thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: single-tenant MAPLEHEALTH — streaming p99 stalls detected in us-east-1. metric=streaming.response_time.p99 > 12s for last 10m, ~6% of requests affected. Severity: page. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-stalls

ashley: ack, on it. tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml. @vikram can you join?

vikram: on my way, grabbing metrics now. seen large cluster of long-prefix sessions from maplehealth, looks like many requests with huge prompt blobs (medical export JSONs). prefix_len distribution shows long tail.

ashley: logs show streaming producer goroutines piling up, backpressure on conveyor. snippet: 
```
2026-03-14T00:12:48Z conveyor: enqueue latency=36ms backlog=172 active_slots=64
streaming: write stall after 8500 tokens, kvcache miss rate spike=0.78
```

luis-ml: hypothesis: huge prefix caused KV cache churn + large attention windows -> kernel path fallback + slow token emit. also noticed many concurrent small user sessions (lots of short-lived connections) causing scheduling overhead.

jun: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable per-tenant soft rate-limit, 2) route maplehealth to a smaller model variant for now, 3) enable streaming buffer fallback so partial frames deliver sooner. which order?

ashley: do 1 + 3 immediately, 2 if still bad. I'll apply soft rate-limit at broker layer. command: 
```
# throttle maplehealth to 40 rps (soft)
redwoodctl tenants throttle set --tenant maplehealth --rps 40 --scope streaming --soft
```

ashley: applying now...

incident-bot: action taken: throttle applied by ashley at 1998881298.

vikram: enabling fallback_stream_buffer for tenant (will let consumers get partial frames): 
```
redwoodctl feature-flag set --tenant maplehealth fallback_stream_buffer=on
```

luis-ml: also toggled kvcache eviction policy from lru -> size-priority for maplehealth to reduce churn.

emily: CS update: notified MapleHealth engineering that we're investigating and temporarily throttling their streaming rate to mitigate stalls. they're seeing partial responses but prefer availability over latency.

caroline-cs: customer notes they started a batch job yesterday sending ~200 concurrent sessions with multi-MB JSON payloads. they will pause if needed.

vikram: after throttle + buffer, p99 dropped from ~13.4s -> ~6.1s in 6m. tail stalls reduced but still above SLO (5s).

ashley: ok escalate to model fallback. we'll route new requests to smaller quantized variant (gptx-13b-q4) for maplehealth, keep older sessions draining. command: 
```
redwoodctl routing update --tenant maplehealth --from model=gptx-70b --to model=gptx-13b-q4 --drain 60s
```

incident-bot: routing update queued by ashley at 1998881389.

jun: confirming routing switch applied. telemetry shows per-token CPU usage down and p99 at ~3.2s after switchover for new sessions. legacy sessions still draining cause occasional spikes.

vikram: found a second contributor: many prompts include inline base64 attachments, our tokenizer expands those into extremely long token sequences. we should add a prompt prefilter for base64 detection and warn the tenant.

luis-ml: I can put a guard in the pre-tokenizer to truncate long encoded blobs and return a warning field in streaming metadata. quick patch ready, will canary to staging then prod if OK.

ashley: good. canary and roll. in the meantime, keep rate-limit in place and leave routing to 13b.

emily: CS updated customer: we recommended pausing the batch job and removing attachments or using presigned storage references. Customer agreed to pause; they'll send a sanitized test payload.

caroline-cs: MapleHealth thanks the team, wants postmortem and the ETA for a non-throttled solution.

jun: handoff: I'm taking day oncall from night. summary for next shift: maplehealth p99 streaming stalls caused by huge prompt payloads + KV cache churn + concurrency; mitigations: soft throttle (40 rps), fallback_stream_buffer enabled, route new sessions to gptx-13b-q4, kvcache policy tweak; ongoing: pretokenizer guard patch (luis), postmortem & long-term model routing policy (vikram).

ashley: adding incident channel note and creating ticket: INC-1998 MapleHealth streaming stalls - owner: vikram, eng-runtime action, eng-ml patch.

vikram: I'll own postmortem and long-term fixes: 1) pretokenizer guard, 2) tenant-aware caching tiers, 3) routing policy to prefer smaller model for bursty workflows.

luis-ml: starting canary of pretokenizer guard now. I'll post results in 15m.

emily: thanks team. I'll follow up with customer once postmortem draft ready.

jun: last check before closing pager: p99 stabilized at ~2.9s over 10m window, error rate normal. I'm removing paging status but keeping channel open until postmortem.

incident-bot: Pager status: resolved -> monitoring. closed at 1998884721.

ashley: handoff complete. leaving notes in runbook.

vikram: assigning follow-ups in Jira: RDW-5543 (pretokenizer guard), RDW-5544 (tenant cache tiers), RDW-5545 (routing heuristics).

jun: thanks all.
